scope.reason: The rebuild tree src_new/ + tests_new/ is the product being cleaned, ahead of the src_new -> src cutover. The legacy src/ and tests/ trees are slated for deletion once the rebuild is fully working and are kept only for reference, so they are readable to explain why a rebuild module ports an odd behaviour, but are never swept and never filed against. docs/audits/ is sealed rather than referenced: it holds nine prior findings reports, and a sweeper that reads one has stopped being blind, which makes the pass compromised by definition. Both ledgers are sealed for the same reason. The governance artifacts (project description, requirements, user stories, architecture) are readable because activities 0 and 2 exist to compare the code against them. tmp/ is scratch and never a product.

0.title: Specs — requirements and user stories exist, are testable, and cover the code

passes.direction_note: Reconnaissance only — no source or test file was touched.
passes.note: Seed reconnaissance sweep — one subagent, briefed on the full flag catalogue and the whole scope, deliberately shallow and time-boxed. Returned 22 findings across 12 flag classes and reported no contamination. This is a sample, not an inventory: it satisfies no gate and makes no completeness claim. Its only purpose is to give every activity a non-empty denominator, so that activity 0's and 1.a's verification is not vacuous by construction. Findings carry the sweeper's own confidence rating and are unverified — each is checked under Phase 2.5 by the activity that owns it, before any fix.

Pass 1 swept the code->spec direction blind and returned 25 spec-gaps across 12 subsystems, but rediscovered NEITHER item in the frozen denominator. Both misses are the same class, and it is a class the brief did not ask for: the sweeper hunted BEHAVIOUR WITH NO REQUIREMENT and found it well, but never looked for requirements that contradict EACH OTHER, or that fall silent on a state the system can actually reach. CD-0001 is two acceptance criteria of one story disagreeing about the same event; CD-0024 is an acceptance criterion saying nothing about a reachable case. Neither is 'undocumented behaviour', so neither was in scope for how the sweep was framed. Pass 2 brief: read each story's acceptance criteria AGAINST EACH OTHER and against the requirements they cite, and for every criterion ask which reachable states its Given clause fails to cover. Method guidance only — name no locations.
passes.direction_note: Analysis only; activity 0 changes no code. No source or test file touched.

passes.note: Fresh sweeper, not a continuation of pass 1's — that agent knows what it found and, after the comparison, what it missed. Depth per the protocol: read files end to end rather than searching them, follow call chains across module boundaries. Plus pass 1's method correction: read acceptance criteria against each other and hunt for silences, not only for undocumented behaviour.

defects.title: Per-tool availability tracking was dropped as YAGNI, orphaning the four spec items written in terms of it
defects.evidence: The rebuild keeps only a per-poll integer: count_available_tools(resolved_paths, definitions) returns how many tools are available NOW (sync_once.py:42-59). No per-tool status is carried in SyncState across polls, so no transition can be observed. The drop was deliberate — docs/architecture_implementation_plan.md records 'Per-tool availability-status transition logging — old tool_status.py logged available/unavailable/disabled transitions; the new tree keeps only count_available_tools (the two-tool guard's consumer). Dropped as YAGNI; document the reduced observability. [decision: drop]'. But four spec items are written in terms of that state: US-11 AC-2 ('Given an agentic_tool's status was available at the previous poll and its directory has become missing'), AC-3 ('Given ... was unavailable at the previous poll and its directory is present ... at the current poll'), AC-5 (status-transition logging), and NFR-12 ('The daemon shall log an agentic_tool's status only on transitions (startup counts as a transition), not on every poll'). US-11 also carries a five-column status table (Configured / Enabled / Root reachable / Logged on entry) describing a per-tool status model the rebuild does not have.
defects.impact: The drop was assessed as costing observability. It cost more than that: it removed the state three acceptance criteria and one NFR are phrased against, so those items cannot be implemented or verified as written — they are not merely unbuilt. This is the root of CD-0001: US-11 AC-3's re-extension rule needs to know a tool just returned, and nothing knows that. Resolving CD-0001 by tuning the glitch threshold would paper over a missing concept; resolving it by restoring availability tracking reopens a decision recorded as closed. Either way it is the spec owner's call, not an implementation detail.

defects.title: Archive GC permanently deletes preserved user bytes on a hard-coded age/rate schedule
defects.evidence: KEEP_ALL_WITHIN_DAYS=7, DOWNSAMPLE_DAYS=30, RETAIN_DAYS=365, KEEP_PER_DAY_RECENT=4, KEEP_PER_DAY_OLD=1 (lines 37-41). _apply_tiered_policy -> `else: to_delete.append(entry)` (198); _remove_entry: `if path.is_dir(): shutil.rmtree(path) else: path.unlink()` (229-233). Asserted by test_artifact_archive.py::test_entries_beyond_retention_are_deleted and three siblings.
defects.impact: NFR-07 bounds archive growth by restricting CREATION only; it says nothing about deleting entries legitimately created. US-05 AC-2 requires files be 'moved to archive — never rm'd' and makes the archive the recovery mechanism. No requirement authorises destroying archive entries or sets 7/30/365 days or 4/1 per day. The guarantee the project sells hardest — no user content is ever destroyed — is silently time-limited by five unagreed constants.

defects.title: The daemon voluntarily exits after five consecutive failed polls
defects.evidence: DEFAULT_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 5, commented 'this many consecutive ones in a row downs the daemon (FR-02)'; watch: `consecutive_exceptions += 1 ... if consecutive_exceptions >= max_consecutive_failures: return EXIT_RUNTIME_FAILURE` (88-95).
defects.impact: FR-02 is cited but is about fault isolation BETWEEN artifacts and tools — it authorises continuing, never stopping. US-07 AC-3 requires the daemon resume 'without operator intervention'; NFR-04 and NFR-17 agree. NFR-10 defines a distinct runtime-failure exit code but never says what triggers it. At the 2s default interval a recoverable condition kills the unattended daemon in ~10 seconds.

defects.title: Hard input-size caps refuse and freeze legitimate artifacts, and are explicitly non-configurable
defects.evidence: MAX_PARSE_BYTES=16MiB, MAX_FRONTMATTER_BYTES=256KiB, MAX_SKILL_AUXILIARY_FILES=1000, MAX_SKILL_FOLDER_BYTES=32MiB, MAX_YAML_ALIAS_RESOLUTIONS=10000 (33-53). Module docstring: 'The bounds are deliberately constants, not configuration.' ParserBoundsExceeded subclasses MalformedSurfaceError so the read phase records a ParseFailure -> FreezeArtifact.
defects.impact: No FR or NFR mentions input size or DoS resistance. FR-11 authorises freezing when metadata is MALFORMED; a 40MiB well-formed skill folder is not malformed. A large but legitimate skill (reference PDFs, a dataset sample) is excluded from sync forever, reported only as a freeze. Five thresholds decide what the product will sync, with no requirement behind them.

defects.title: Writing one MCP slot rewrites the whole shared config file, destroying the user's comments
defects.evidence: Module docstring: 'Round-trip preserves key order and data; it does not preserve comments.' serialize re-emits the whole deserialized root via json.dumps or the hand-rolled _emit_toml_table (48-56); keyed_map_slot.write_slot calls it on the whole root (94).
defects.impact: US-01 AC-5 forbids exactly this: 'existing key order, comments, and quoting style are preserved where the underlying format permits' — TOML permits comments. US-04 AC-4 repeats it for renames; the integration protocol requires keys outside map_key_path be preserved byte-for-byte. The markdown dialect honours this via a ruamel round-trip loader; this codec does not. The user's own annotations in ~/.codex/config.toml — a file agents_sync does not own — are deleted, and only the slot fragment is archived.

defects.title: Cursor is declared to support agent and skill, which US-13 explicitly denies
defects.evidence: VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR. cursor.py declares five recipes including SurfaceRecipe('agent', 'cursor_agents_dir', ..., Layout.DIRECTORY) at line 29 and SurfaceRecipe('skill', 'cursor_skills_dir', ..., Layout.SKILL_FOLDER) at line 60. US-13 line 45 reads: "Cursor's adapter ships with `rules`, `slash_command`, and `mcp_server` support — no `agent`, no `skill` — because Cursor has no file-based equivalents for the latter two." US-10 AC-3's worked example lists cursor as {rules, slash_command, mcp_server}.
defects.impact: The daemon materialises the user's entire agent and skill library into two directories the spec says Cursor cannot read: dead files on disk, doubled write and archive volume for every agent/skill change, and Cursor added to every conflict and tiebreak group for types it does not consume.

defects.title: A from-scratch global-rules file is created under AGENTS.md, not the tool's create-name
defects.evidence: VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR. read_tool_surfaces.py:373-375: `# FR-10: a rules file that does not exist yet is created under the highest-precedence declared filename (``AGENTS.md`` where offered). return resolved.path / recipe.candidate_filenames[0]`. claude.py declares candidate_filenames=('AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md'). US-14 AC-5 — marked [x] DONE — requires the opposite: 'the file is created under that tool's create-name (the lowest-precedence / legacy standard name: CLAUDE.md for claude, AGENTS.md for codex and opencode)'. FR-10 governs DETECTION precedence, not creation, so the comment misattributes its own rule. SurfaceRecipe has no create-name field at all.
defects.impact: A fresh Claude Code install receives its synced global rules at a filename Claude may not load, so the rules appear to sync but have no effect — the precise failure US-14 AC-5 exists to prevent. The create-name concept has also been dropped from the data model, so there is currently no way to express it.

defects.title: Tool availability is 'any one directory exists', and reachability is judged again, differently, per kind
defects.evidence: `if any(directory.exists() for directory in directories): available += 1`. Contrast reconcile_known.py:150-176 _has_vanished_surface, whose docstring says judging per tool 'would not do'. Two coexisting definitions of reachable.
defects.impact: US-11 AC-1 defines the opposite quantifier — a tool is unavailable when ANY of its configured directories is missing. The safety count gating every destructive operation (US-07 AC-5) is computed by a rule the spec inverts, so a half-uninstalled tool inflates the available count and re-enables destructive polls. Overlaps CD-0025 (no per-tool status exists at all).

defects.title: The canonical rewrites user content: CRLF to LF, trailing newlines collapsed, fields stripped, tool lists sorted
defects.evidence: canonical_store.py:174 persists document.normalised().to_dict(). normalised(): name=self.name.strip(), description=self.description.strip(), body=_normalise_body(self.body), tools=tuple(sorted(self.tools)), disallowed_tools=tuple(sorted(...)). _normalise_body: replace CRLF/CR with LF, rstrip newlines, then add exactly one. Pinned by test_canonical_document.py::test_body_line_endings_normalised_to_lf_with_single_trailing_newline.
defects.impact: NFR-06 requires round-tripping 'preserve the original bytes on the source'; NFR-16 requires reading into canonical form 'shall not lose user-authored information'; US-01 AC-5 requires preserving formatting on rewrite. On Windows (first-class since v0.3) every synced artifact is silently converted to LF, showing up as a whole-file diff in the user's own version control. Sorting a tools list changes semantics for any tool treating order as precedence. Note auxiliary_files explicitly exempts itself from newline normalisation; the document body has no such exemption written anywhere.

defects.title: Skill rename rmtrees the old folder having archived only SKILL.md; skill removal orphans the folder
defects.evidence: Independently found by this sweep as a SPEC gap; the same code is already filed as a defect (CD-0012 rename, CD-0013 removal, CD-0017 docstring). The spec angle is new: US-05 AC-2 requires that on removal 'each other agentic_tool's file OR FOLDER is moved to archive — never rm'd', and US-01 AC-9 makes auxiliary files first-class synced content, so the archive scope and the delete scope of a folder-layout artifact are specified and the code matches neither.
defects.impact: Corroborates CD-0012 from the spec direction and supplies the requirement the fix must satisfy. No requirement permits rmtree of unarchived bytes, nor an orphaned folder after removal.

defects.title: An unreadable file or transient I/O error on one tool freezes the artifact on every tool
defects.evidence: `except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, MalformedSurfaceError) as error: return SurfaceObservation(..., parsed=ParseFailure(f'unreadable surface: {error}'))` (214-219); reconcile_known.py:60-61 turns any single ParseFailure in the group into FreezeArtifact for the whole artifact.
defects.impact: FR-11 authorises freezing exactly one case: 'When the metadata is malformed such that content cannot be parsed'. A permission error, a mid-write partial read, or an oversize file is not malformed metadata. US-03 AC-11 scopes freeze the same way; US-07 AC-3 and FR-02 point the other way for I/O errors. One antivirus lock stops that artifact syncing on all tools.

defects.title: An `agents-sync prune` subcommand exists and the daemon runs an archive GC every 24 hours
defects.evidence: subcommands.add_parser('prune', ...); _dispatch routes it to _prune(config); run_daemon passes run_gc=lambda: _gc_once(state_dir); poll_daemon.py:30 DEFAULT_GC_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 24*60*60, fired on the tick (100-102).
defects.impact: US-12 defines the one-shot CLI surface as export and import only; the project description says 'Continuous daemon operation, plus one-shot CLI subcommands for portable export and import'. No requirement mentions prune, a GC cadence, or reclaimed-bytes logging. A user-visible command and a background destructive timer ship with no acceptance criterion, so neither the cadence nor the command's arguments, exit codes, or (absent) dry-run can be verified or safely changed.

defects.title: The on-disk state and canonical formats do not match the documented layout
defects.evidence: state.json is written as {'schema_version': 1, 'records': {<id>: {'name','canonical_digest','surfaces':{<tool>:{'location':{'path'|'file'+'slot'},'content_digest'}}}}}. canonical_store.py:37 CANONICAL_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1; a file whose schema_version is not exactly 1 is quarantined (111-114). A third directory <state_dir>/quarantine/ holds <name>.<monotonic_ns>.<random>.corrupt.
defects.impact: docs/project_description.md documents a different layout as the contract: schema_version 4, key 'customization_artifacts' not 'records', per-tool 'agentic_tools' with 'digests'. US-10 AC-4 pins the state path as state.customization_artifacts[<id>].agentic_tools[<name>]. An install upgraded to the rebuild quarantines its schema-4 state and starts empty, re-projecting everything. The documented layout is the only description a recovery script has.

defects.title: An intent whose surfaces share one write file is refused every poll, forever
defects.evidence: `write_files = [target_file(s) for s in surfaces]; if len(set(write_files)) != len(write_files): raise IntentAbortError(...)`, called from project_canonical, adopt_new_artifact and rename_artifact; caught in execute_sync_plan/__init__.py:99 into execution.failed and retried identically next poll.
defects.impact: No requirement covers it. US-06 AC-6 (cited in the docstring) is about atomicity across conflict losers. US-04 AC-5 and US-03 AC-8 define refusals for slug collisions between DIFFERENT artifacts and require a structured error naming the colliding ids — this is one artifact with two surfaces, a different condition with a less informative outcome. A reasonable configuration (two tools anchored under ~/.gemini) stalls permanently with no diagnosis.

defects.title: Writing an MCP slot replaces any non-object value at the map path, discarding it unarchived
defects.evidence: `child = node.get(key); if not isinstance(child, dict): child = {}; node[key] = child`, justified in comment as 'loses no artifact data — it self-heals a structurally-broken shared file'.
defects.impact: A user's `mcpServers: null`, `mcp: "disabled"`, or a list at that key is deleted with no archive entry and no warning. The integration protocol requires keys outside map_key_path be preserved byte-for-byte but is silent on the map key itself holding something unexpected; NFR-01 forbids losing user-authored content 'under any operation'; US-05 AC-1 would require archiving anything displaced. The 'loses no artifact data' justification concerns MANAGED artifacts; the discarded value is user-authored config.

defects.title: An @import chain deeper than ten levels freezes the rules artifact
defects.evidence: _MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH = 10; `if _depth > _MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH: raise RulesImportError('rules @import nesting exceeds maximum depth')`; read_tool_surfaces.py:195-196 turns it into ParseFailure.
defects.impact: US-15 AC-1 requires transitive depth-first resolution with no stated bound. US-15 AC-4 enumerates exactly three failure cases — missing/unreadable file, file outside the rules directory, import cycle — and a depth cap is none of them. Cycles are already caught separately by _seen_targets, so the cap protects against nothing that is not already handled.

defects.title: A non-canonical but valid UUID is treated as absent, so a new id is minted and the file rewritten
defects.evidence: `if parsed.version != 4 or str(parsed) != value: raise InvalidArtifactId(...)`. recover_identity.py:75-81 swallows that into False, so _recover_id returns None -> AdoptNewArtifact -> mint_artifact_id(). An uppercase UUID, a brace-wrapped UUID, or a UUIDv1/v7 is rejected.
defects.impact: FR-11 requires that when the id tag 'is present and well-formed' the daemon 'shall not mint a new id, and shall not misattribute the artifact'. An uppercase spelling of the same UUID is arguably well-formed. Case-normalising a UUID by hand causes an identity split: a fresh id is minted, the artifact re-adopted, and the two copies can then collide by slug. FR-11's guarantee has an unwritten exception.

defects.title: OS sidecar files inside a skill folder are silently excluded from sync and deleted on the target
defects.evidence: _IGNORED_TREE_NAMES = frozenset({'.DS_Store'}), _IGNORED_TREE_PREFIXES = ('._',); read_auxiliary_files skips any path with a matching part. Module docstring justifies it as 'The legacy tree excluded these too; keeping the rule preserves that behaviour across cutover.'
defects.impact: US-01 AC-9 states the opposite without exception: 'When ANY file inside the folder is added, modified, moved, or deleted ... Auxiliary files are propagated verbatim.' A user file legitimately named ._template is invisible to sync and is destroyed on the target by the folder swap, since the staged tree is built only from the canonical. The exclusion set is also the kind of list that grows silently unless the rule is written down.

defects.title: The canonical rewrites the user's environment-variable reference syntax
defects.evidence: `for field in ('env','auth','headers'): changes[field] = _restyle_env_map(changes[field], _CANONICAL_ENV_STYLE)`; _ENV_REFERENCE_TOKEN_PATTERN matches ${env:N}, ${N} and {env:N} interchangeably; render.py restyles with spelling.env_reference_style, a single per-tool constant rather than the observed spelling.
defects.impact: NFR-06 requires round-trip preserve 'the original bytes on the source'. A user who wrote $TOKEN or {env:TOKEN} in a Claude config gets ${TOKEN} written back. The same dialect carefully preserves observed FIELD spellings via per_tool_only/_record_alias — the mechanism simply is not applied to VALUE syntax. The tests assert the canonical style rather than the authored one, so they cannot catch it.

defects.title: The MCP dialect rejects a range of well-formed slots as malformed, freezing the artifact
defects.evidence: Five independent checks raise MalformedSurfaceError: two spellings of one alias family (url + httpUrl), mixed stdio/http fields, command-as-array with args, a boolean or float timeout, and any slot value that is not JSON-representable (an unquoted TOML date in Codex's config.toml). Twelve-plus tests pin them.
defects.impact: The integration protocol lists the canonical fields and per-tool aliases and says only 'On a malformed slot, the artifact is skipped with a structured warning'. It never defines which field combinations are malformed, and it expects tools to spell fields differently. FR-11 authorises freezing on malformed metadata but leaves malformed undefined; here it is strict enough to reject configurations the tools themselves load fine.

defects.title: A corrupt state.json is quarantined and the daemon restarts from an empty state
defects.evidence: `except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as error: quarantine_corrupt_file(...); return SyncState()`. _record_from_dict raises on any missing key, so strictness is deliberate. Pinned by test_sync_state_store.py::test_a_record_missing_required_keys_is_quarantined.
defects.impact: US-09 AC-4 specifies quarantine-and-rebuild for exactly one artefact — THE CANONICAL — not state.json. US-09 AC-3 says state lost from a clobbered write 'is recomputed from disk on the next poll', recomputed rather than discarded wholesale. One damaged byte triggers a full-library re-projection and a burst of archive entries on every tool. Whether state.json is disposable is a recovery-semantics decision nobody wrote down.

defects.title: Archive entry names carry a random token, so they do not match the documented archive layout
defects.evidence: `unique_token = uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]; timestamp = ...strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S-%fZ'); return side_dir / f'{entry_name}.{unique_token}.{timestamp}'`. The GC parses only the final dot-segment, which makes the token position load-bearing.
defects.impact: US-05 AC-1 gives the layout as a literal contract: archive/<artifact_id>/<tool_name>/<original-filename>.<ISO-UTC-timestamp>, repeated verbatim in US-03 AC-1, US-06 AC-1 and the integration protocol. US-05's Notes name the timestamp itself as the collision remedy. The archive layout is the user's documented recovery interface; a glob or sort written against the documented pattern misses or misorders every real entry.

defects.title: The configuration file contract — location, required table, and keys — is undefined in the spec
defects.evidence: Reads <config-dir>/agents-sync/config.toml and requires a top-level [agents-sync] table: `if _CONFIG_TABLE_KEY not in data: raise ConfigurationError(...)`. Honours exactly three settings plus one path-override key per surface. No per-tool enable/disable key exists.
defects.impact: US-07 AC-7 presupposes a config file and names two of its defects but never states where it lives, what its table is called, or what keys exist. US-10 AC-2 requires a matching [agentic_tools.<name>] config block — a nested shape the code does not implement — and US-10 AC-9 requires an `enabled = false` key that does not exist. The single interface the user configures the product through is defined only by its implementation.

defects.title: Transient I/O errors — including every PermissionError — are retried six times inside the poll
defects.evidence: _RETRY_ATTEMPTS=6, _RETRY_BASE_DELAY_SECONDS=0.02, _RETRY_MAX_DELAY_SECONDS=0.30, jittered by random.uniform(0.7,1.3); _is_transient_error: `if isinstance(error, PermissionError): return True` on every platform.
defects.impact: NFR-04 and US-07 AC-3 promise recovery BETWEEN polls, not retries within one. US-01 AC-11 and US-05 AC-4 treat 'permission denied' as a failure to report and re-attempt next poll — the code instead treats it as transient and blocks ~1s per operation. NFR-02's latency guarantee and NFR-09's linearity bound are both invisible to a sleeping retry loop.

defects.title: Slug derivation invents names: a shared placeholder for unnameable artifacts, an -item suffix for Windows device names
defects.evidence: _PLACEHOLDER_SLUG = 'converted'; `if not slug: return _PLACEHOLDER_SLUG`; `if slug.upper() in _WINDOWS_RESERVED_BASENAMES: return f'{slug}-item'`. candidate_key pairs the kind with this slug, so the slug is the reconciliation key.
defects.impact: The glossary defines Slug only as 'the filesystem-friendly form of a name'; the integration protocol lists filename-character restrictions as a POSSIBLE FUTURE layout flag, i.e. explicitly not yet specified. A user with purely CJK or emoji artifact names gets every such artifact collapsed onto the single key 'converted' and rejected as a collision (US-03 AC-8), which reads as a bug with no spec to appeal to.

defects.title: A surface whose stat() races loses every freshness tiebreak by being dated to the epoch
defects.evidence: `try: return path.stat().st_mtime except OSError: return 0.0`, docstring: 'The epoch sentinel makes the racing surface lose any freshest-content tiebreak this poll.' freshest() sorts on -modified_time (winner_selection.py:28-35). Same code as CD-0005, filed there as a silent swallow; the spec angle is separate.
defects.impact: US-06 AC-1 defines the winner as 'the changed agentic_tool with the most recent mtime' and AC-4 defines the tie-break by tool name; neither contemplates an unreadable mtime. No requirement says an unstattable surface should be deemed oldest rather than excluded or deferred, and NFR-13 would require a structured report of the condition; none is emitted.
